description:
Find out how this repository signs in, so a journey can reach pages behind a login.
USE THIS when a journey you are about to record or gate requires being logged in.

⚠ YOU CAN CREATE THE ACCOUNT. YOU CANNOT READ ITS PASSWORD BACK. Creating one generates an email and a random password for a user that exists NOWHERE yet, so an agent key that mints one gains nothing: it holds a login to an app where that user has never been seeded. Revealing the password of an account that by now DOES exist is a different thing, and it stays behind an interactive sign-in, in the dashboard.

HOW IT WORKS: calling this creates the account if the repository has none, and returns the existing one if it has. Someone then adds that user to the seed script, so it exists in every environment, including each pull request's own database, which is why a copied staging password would not work.

ONCE THE ACCOUNT EXISTS, DO TWO THINGS:
1. Add the user to the seed, reading the password from `process.env.TADA_TEST_PASSWORD`, and tell the human to set that variable wherever their app seeds.
2. Reference the values symbolically in every step, in a journey and in a flow alike: `fill Email with {{secret.TADA_TEST_EMAIL}}`, `fill Password with {{secret.TADA_TEST_PASSWORD}}`. NEVER paste the literal password into a step, a file, or a commit. A passing journey is written back into the repository as a flow file, so a literal typed here would be committed and reviewed; Tada refuses to write the file at all rather than commit one, and the substitution happens on the runner at the moment of typing.

You never need to read either value yourself. The runner substitutes them at the moment of typing, and the stored journey keeps the placeholders.
It is safe to call more than once. An existing account is returned unchanged, never replaced.

WITH A `role`, IT ASKS FOR A RESIDENT INSTEAD: one of Tada’s own users living in your app in that role (admin, client, staff), so a journey can act as that person.
Tada makes the user and returns its email and password once. Where Tada already has an admin inside your app, Tada adds that user to your app itself, through your invite screen the way a person would, and the answer says so (planting). Where Tada has nobody inside yet, the answer says this first user is added from your side (the seed script, the invite screen, or an admin page).
ALREADY HAVE A USER SEEDED FOR TADA? Pass `role` with `email` and `password` and Tada adopts that login instead of making one. Tada seals the password and types it itself.
A resident is made once and reused by every run after it. Asking again for the same role returns the same resident, with its status and what happens next.
Tada keeps every resident's password and types it at every sign-in. Steps reference a resident as {{secret.TADA_<ROLE>_EMAIL}} and {{secret.TADA_<ROLE>_PASSWORD}}, or with "role: <role>" on a step.

email.description: Only with `role`, and only when you ALREADY seeded a user for Tada in the app: its address. Tada adopts that login rather than making one.

environment.description: Only with `role`: which environment, by name (e.g. "staging"). Leave it out unless Tada asks which one.

password.description: The password of the login named by `email`. Tada seals it and never hands it back.

repo.description: The repository, as "owner/name" (e.g. "acme/storefront"). Must already be connected to Tada.

role.description: Ask for a RESIDENT in this role instead of the repository test account: the app’s own word for it, such as "admin", "client" or "staff".

name: setup_test_account
